title: code-review-pr-scratchpad-alex-morgan
content:
PR: refactor: continuous-batcher + kv-cache pruning (#428)
Author: Priya Nair
Reviewer: Alex Morgan (scratchpad)
Related linear: LIN-1124 (batcher perf), LIN-1178 (kv-cache stability)
Slack thread: #CR-batcher (see context link above)

----
High-level summary:
- This PR consolidates the continuous batching logic into a single Batcher class (batcher.py) and moves the KV cache pruning heuristics into kv_cache_manager.cpp/cpp-bindings.
- Goal: reduce duplicate scheduling logic, improve cache eviction correctness under high concurrency, and expose a compact API for the runtime to request cache maintenance.
- Adds new metrics: batcher.enqueue_latency_ms, batcher.batch_size_distribution, kv_cache.prune_cycles, kv_cache.eviction_reclaimed_bytes.

----
Files of interest (quick list):
- batcher.py (huge rewrite, ~420 LOC)
- grpc_handler.go (integration points updated to use new batcher.enqueue API)
- kv_cache_manager.cpp / bindings.cc (new pruning logic)
- tests/test_batcher.py (new tests)
- tests/integration/test_kv_cache_eviction.py (flaky locally)
- Makefile / BUILD changes for new native lib

----
Initial concerns / risks:
- Threading model: kv_cache_manager is native C++ called via bindings; need to confirm GIL release and thread-safety for concurrent prune triggers from Python runtime. Look for Py_BEGIN_ALLOW_THREADS / Py_END_ALLOW_THREADS or equivalent.
- Memory safety: new eviction algorithm touches shared buffers; audit for use-after-free when Rust/C++ objects are referenced by Python objects.
- Backwards compatibility: grpc_handler.go changed to call enqueue(ctx, req, opts) with new opts flag (allow_partial=true). Ensure older callers are not broken.
- Metrics cardinality: new tags on metrics might increase cardinality in Prometheus; verify label set is bounded.
- Testing: flaky integration test for eviction on CI; needs stable reproducer.

----
Checklist (must pass before merge):
- [ ] Unit tests: all new tests pass locally and in CI (pytest -q, coverage unchanged)
- [ ] Integration tests: re-run flaky test with stress harness (see notes)
- [ ] Thread-safety audit: confirm GIL behavior in bindings and annotate code with comments explaining locking strategy
- [ ] Memory audit: run ASAN/Valgrind on native lib during integration test run (CI job optional but recommended)
- [ ] Metrics: add tests that assert metric labels are within whitelist (prevent unbounded tags)
- [ ] API compatibility: add compatibility shim for enqueue(old_signature) to avoid breaking Dedicated runtime until rollout
- [ ] Performance benchmark: run perf harness (scripts/perf/batcher_bench.py) and compare to baseline (perf artifacts attached)
- [ ] Rollout plan: add canary flag under feature_flags.json and rollout doc snippet (see "Rollout" section below)

----
Suggested code-level comments / small changes:
- batcher.py: function schedule_batch() still iterates over waiting queue with two nested loops; consider replacing with deque + single pass to compute target_batch_size. Avoid calling sleep() in hot path, use event-based wakeups.
- batcher.py: add explicit type hints for enqueue() to help mypy and future refactors; eg -> def enqueue(self, req: Request, allow_partial: bool = False) -> Future[Response]
- grpc_handler.go: check error paths when enqueue returns ErrQueueFull; currently those errors map to 500. Convert to 429 + metrics.increment("enqueue_rejected")
- kv_cache_manager.cpp: add comment about reclamation step ordering; current code reclaims LRU buckets without checking active references. Add a guard that queries ref_count_map for each key before freeing.
- bindings.cc: ensure we call PyGILState_Ensure when creating new Python objects from C++ threads (or use proper GIL state management).

----
Refactor ideas (medium-sized, not required for this PR):
- Move batching policy into a strategy interface (BatchPolicy) so we can A/B experiment new policies without hot reloading core; reduces churn in Batcher class.
- Introduce a weakref-based lease model for KV entries: when a request references a KV slot, it holds a lightweight lease object to prevent eviction until response completion. This avoids ref_count_map races.
- Separate metrics emission into a thin MetricsEmitter interface so native code can push metrics in a bounded manner (prevents dynamic label sets).

----
Follow-ups / TODOs (assign & track):
- [LIN-1178] (Priya) Stabilize integration test for eviction. Repro script: scripts/test_repro/kv_eviction_repro.py (note: uses local docker image). Target: 2026-01-10 (missed) -> reopen and triage.
- (Alex) Add compatibility shim for enqueue(old_signature) and add regression test in tests/test_grpc_compat.py. ETA: 2026-02-05 (in-progress).
- (Ethan) Run ASAN job in a nightly CI pipeline for native libs; link: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/native-asan.
- (SRE) Validate new metrics ingestion: ops@redwood to confirm no high-cardinality explosion.

----
Testing notes / how I tested locally:
- Ran pytest -k batcher -q; unit tests passed.
- Ran mini perf harness (scripts/perf/batcher_local_bench.py) on dev-machine (A100) -> observed 6% median latency regression for short sequences vs baseline. Need to investigate scheduling overhead.
- Reproduced flaky eviction locally with stress runner: seeds vary; suspect race in prune loop when concurrent request holds a C++ pointer after Python drops reference.

----
Questions for author (Priya):
1) Can you point to the binding(s) where we release the GIL during long prune ops? I couldn't find Py_BEGIN_ALLOW_THREADS in the new bindings.cc.
2) Was the metric label set intentionally open (cache_key_type) or should we provide a sanitized label?
3) Are there performance expectations / SLOs for the new batcher changes documented anywhere (perf deck link)?

----
Action items before approving:
- [ ] Priya: add GIL handling comment + small test that runs prune from a thread and asserts no Python crashes.
- [ ] Priya: add guard in prune to check reference counts before freeing (even if cheap).
- [ ] Alex: add compatibility shim and unit tests for grpc_handler.go changes.
- [ ] Ethan: add ASAN nightly job and post link in PR description.
- [ ] SRE/Ops: sanity-check metrics ingestion after merge in staging.

----
Rollout suggestion:
- Canary rollout on Dedicated clusters only (small subset of regions) behind feature flag: enable_batcher_v2 = true
- Monitor: enqueue_latency_ms p95, kv_cache.prune_cycles, error rates from grpc_handler.go (429/500), and memory usage for native lib (RSS, peak).
- Failure action: automatic rollback of feature flag and revert batcher to previous path via canary routing.

----
Notes & references:
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/410 (previous attempt at continuous batcher)
- Perf harness: scripts/perf/batcher_bench.py
- Repro scripts: scripts/test_repro/kv_eviction_repro.py
- CI job for native: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/native-asan

----
Personal quick judgement:
- This is a solid cleanup with sensible API separation. Major risk is native <> python concurrency surface. If author can add the GIL/thread-safety guards and we run ASAN, I'm ok to approve after compatibility shim is in place and flaky test stabilized.

----
Scratchpad (random thoughts / short-term experiments):
- Try a micro-optimization: pre-allocate a small slab for common batch sizes (<=8) to avoid heap churn in enqueue path.
- Add a lightweight backpressure token bucket per-worker rather than global queue cap to reduce global contention during spikes.

----
End of scratchpad.
